models_evaluated: AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) for acute myocardial infarction

links.outcome: AI-ECG AUROC and rule-out safety stratified by sex in prospective ED cohort
links.effect: AUROC 0.875 in women vs 0.871 in men; rule-out sensitivity 98.8% in women vs 99.8% in men; NPV 99.2% vs 99.1%; missed AMI <1% in both sexes.
links.quote: AI-ECG demonstrated comparable discrimination in women and men (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve 0.875 [95% CI: 0.853-0.896] vs 0.871 [95% CI: 0.858-0.883]).

links.outcome: Performance on prospective multicenter external validation cohort
links.effect: Prospective external validation at 18 centers among 8,493 patients showed AUROC 0.875 in women and 0.871 in men, with high rule-out NPV.
links.quote: ROMIAE (Rule-Out Acute Myocardial Infarction Using Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram Analysis) was a prospective external validation study at 18 centers in South Korea.

screen.reason: Prospective multi-center external validation assessing sex-stratified diagnostic performance, rule-out safety, and demographic equity of an AI-ECG model in an ED cohort.
